paper-sobering-look-tabular-generation-2.summary: This paper critiques the evaluation protocols used to benchmark deep generative models for tabular data, showing that widely-used fidelity metrics like C2ST and TREND can be gamed by trivial fully-factorised baselines, and proposes a probabilistic-circuits model (TabPC) that matches diffusion-based state-of-the-art at a fraction of the compute cost. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of many baseline generators across seven benchmark datasets and multiple fidelity/efficiency metrics. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are included as baseline synthesizers among a large set of competing methods evaluated against the authors' proposed TabPC.

paper-balanced-emotion-analysis-syntheti.summary: This paper studies emotion recognition from non-invasive Facial Landmark Trajectories (EMO features) in the ASCERTAIN dataset, classifying emotions into four valence-arousal quadrants and addressing severe class imbalance via SMOTE, a generic GAN, and CTGAN. Four ML classifiers (KNN, SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest) are trained on each augmented dataset, with CTGAN-based augmentation found to produce the least overfitting and the best Random Forest accuracy. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as one of three synthetic-data generators compared, trained with explicit generator/discriminator learning rates and default gradient-penalty settings to oversample the minority emotion classes.

paper-breaking-homogeneity-assumption-sp.summary: This paper addresses severe class imbalance and multimodal failure-type heterogeneity in predictive maintenance data by proposing a specialized multi-generator GAN architecture, where each generator learns to synthesize samples for a distinct failure subtype. Using the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset, the authors compare cost-sensitive learning, undersampling, SMOTE, single-generator GAN augmentation, and their multi-generator approach, finding the latter yields higher PR-AUC and recall. Their generator's design (built on the tabgan library with a WGAN-GP backbone) is described as incorporating mode-specific normalization and a Gumbel-Softmax categorical encoding 'inspired by the CTGAN model,' citing CTGAN as prior art rather than running SDV's implementation.

paper-domain-adaptation-workload-predict.summary: This paper proposes a domain adaptation methodology for CI/CD workload prediction that combines Quantile Mapping and Cross-Temporal Seasonality Transfer to transfer seasonality patterns and duration distributions from non-overlapping time periods of GitHub Actions billing and execution log data. It validates the approach empirically, showing strong correlation of transferred weekly seasonality and reduced distributional error metrics. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only in passing as prior work illustrating that distribution-preserving transformations enable realistic synthetic data generation, an idea the authors say they extend conceptually rather than by using SDV software.

paper-fine-tuning-open-source-2026.summary: This paper compares three LLM fine-tuning techniques—Supervised Fine-Tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA—across open-source models (Llama, Mistral, Phi) for cybersecurity and IT support tasks, finding SFT gives better loss convergence while LoRA/QLoRA cut GPU memory and compute costs substantially with comparable performance. The SDV paper is cited only in passing to support a general claim that domain-specific synthetic data mitigates privacy concerns, with no SDV code or method used anywhere in the study.

paper-gerongnosis-database-diagnosing-de.summary: This paper introduces GeronGnosis, a new Brazilian EEG database for diagnosing Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and mild cognitive impairment, and compares machine learning classifiers (Random Forest, Random Tree, Bayes Network, SVM) on it against the public OpenNeuro dataset. Random Forest with 500 trees achieved the best accuracy (98% on GeronGnosis, 95% on OpenNeuro). To address data scarcity in one experiment, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, described as 'employing autoencoders', to augment the training data.

paper-best-of-n-synthetic-ehr-2026.summary: Asks when clinically impossible rows in synthetic electronic health records can be fixed after generation rather than by retraining, comparing random sampling, naive clipping, best-of-N selection and strict rejection against dataset-specific validity constraints on three public clinical tables, and reporting the privacy cost of each in distance-to-closest-record concentration. CTGAN is one of the two generator backbones the whole study is built on, and CTGAN with best-of-16 selection is the configuration the paper names as the strongest overall trade-off, reaching zero constraint violations on all three datasets.

paper-adverse-drug-reactions-lincs-2026.summary: Predicts adverse drug reactions from LINCS L1000 gene-expression signatures — 978 landmark genes across drug-perturbed cancer cell lines — against 232 ADR categories where the labels are severely imbalanced. SDV-based augmentation is the answer to that imbalance, and the paper's headline result is the neural network *with* SDV augmentation: the library is run to manufacture minority-class rows and the reported gain in generalisation is attributed to it.

paper-stanet-spatiotemporal-attention-ne.summary: This paper proposes STANet, a spatiotemporal attention neural network for predicting aflatoxin M1 contamination levels in raw milk, likely using synthetic or augmented data to support model training and evaluation. The authors evaluate the structural fidelity of their generated/augmented data using SDMetrics' Trend score, which compares statistical associations between real and synthetic feature pairs. SDMetrics' quality report / Trend metric is run as an evaluation tool to assess structural fidelity of the data used.

paper-scalable-multiscale-echo-state-202.summary: The paper proposes a multiscale echo state network architecture with dendritic-style readouts aimed at improving earthquake early warning systems, likely using seismic time-series data to improve detection speed and accuracy. No further methodological detail is available from the metadata alone. CTGAN is cited among the paper's references, but how it is used, if at all, cannot be determined from this evidence.

paper-conditional-tabular-gan-enhanced-2.summary: This paper proposes CTGSM-DNN, a two-stage intrusion detection pipeline for IoT networks that first uses a conditional tabular GAN to synthesize minority-class rare-attack samples, then applies SMOTEENN to clean the augmented dataset before training a DNN classifier, evaluated on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 with 99.90% overall accuracy and 80% rare-attack accuracy. CTGAN is run as the core synthetic data generator producing the rare-attack samples that the whole detection pipeline depends on, using its conditional vector and mode-specific normalization to handle mixed categorical/continuous IoT traffic features.

paper-adhs-el-intrusion-2025.summary: Proposes an intrusion-detection framework that pairs dynamic undersampling with an improved AdvGAN generating adversarial traffic samples, then trains a dynamically weighted classifier ensemble, arguing that augmenting with adversarial rather than merely minority samples both corrects the decision boundary and hardens the model against evasion. CTGAN is one of the eight imbalance-handling baselines run for comparison, reimplemented from a published architecture rather than taken from a library, and is reported as scoring well on adversarial detection while degrading accuracy through overfitting.

paper-improved-generative-adversarial-ne.summary: This paper proposes a modified GAN-based oversampling method for imbalanced classification, introducing similarity and reconstruction losses for the generator to produce higher-quality minority-class samples, evaluated against existing oversampling methods on 20 real-world imbalanced datasets. TGAN is cited only in passing as prior work that adapted GANs to tabular data, and no SDV-family code is run anywhere in the paper.
paper-improved-generative-adversarial-ne.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so cannot confirm whether TGAN was ever run or is purely discussed in related work.

paper-augmentation-method-fatigue-welded.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed data augmentation method for fatigue life prediction of welded structures under two-step variable amplitude loading, embedding the Peng nonlinear damage model as an additional physical loss term (alongside an MMD loss) inside the Conditional Tabular GAN's generator loss function. The augmented model is validated by training four machine learning predictors (KELM, SVM, RF, BP) on the generated data and comparing prediction accuracy against traditional damage models and unaugmented ML models. CTGAN's architecture, condition vector, and generator/discriminator loss functions are directly modified to create this new physics-constrained generator, with its output serving as the training data for all downstream ML models in the study.

paper-comprehensive-evaluation-framework.summary: This paper proposes a holistic evaluation framework for synthetic tabular data that jointly measures fidelity, utility and privacy, and applies it to three open-source medical datasets across five generative models run with and without differential privacy. Among the five models are Gaussian Copula (GC), TVAE and CTGAN, all attributed to the SDV synthesizer suite developed by Patki et al., alongside a Neural Probabilistic Circuit model and a diffusion-based baseline. SDV's Gaussian Copula and TVAE synthesizers (and CTGAN) are run as evaluation subjects, with fidelity, utility and privacy metrics compared across their DP and non-DP variants as a core part of the empirical programme.

paper-augmented-deep-learning-models-202.summary: This paper trains a Multilayer Perceptron to predict compressive strength and thermal conductivity of cementitious composites containing Phase Change Materials and nano-silica aerogel, using a GAN to augment a limited experimental dataset and boost predictive accuracy. In its related-work discussion, the authors cite CTGAN and CopulaGAN as examples of techniques that have demonstrated success augmenting real datasets to improve model performance, without indicating that either was used to build their own GAN. CTGAN is thus invoked only as prior art motivating their data-augmentation approach.

paper-driven-signal-noise-enhancement-20.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning method for denoising scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) images, using a patch-based CycleGAN trained on unpaired short- and long-acquisition-time image sets to improve structural similarity and peak signal-to-noise ratio. The approach enables flexible reconstruction of arbitrary-sized images and reduces required data acquisition time for high-resolution imaging in biological and materials science applications. The work cites the TGAN paper, apparently as background on generative adversarial network architectures, without engaging with it further.
paper-driven-signal-noise-enhancement-20.needs: No full text or citing sentence obtained; cannot confirm how or why TGAN is cited beyond metadata attribution.

paper-fairness-testing-extreme-value-202.summary: This paper proposes extreme counterfactual discrimination (ECD), a fairness criterion grounded in extreme value theory that estimates worst-case disadvantage for protected groups in ML outcomes, along with a randomized sampling algorithm and a new ECD-based bias mitigator, evaluated across ten socially relevant tasks and four ML model types. To generate additional tail samples when a dataset lacks enough relevant instances, the authors run CTGAN and TVAE and evaluate their synthetic output against real data using similarity and downstream-performance metrics (including a logistic-regression detection score) across nine datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are run as evaluation subjects/generators supplying synthetic tail samples for the fairness-testing pipeline, with a detection-based evaluation metric traced to the SDV metrics literature.
paper-fairness-testing-extreme-value-202.needs: Not certain whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or a custom implementation; no explicit import or constructor-parameter evidence is given, though standard naming and lack of architectural description suggest library use.

paper-generating-multi-table-time-2025.summary: This paper introduces RawMed, a framework that synthesizes multi-table, time-series electronic health records by treating raw EHR data as text and compressing it, aiming to preserve all original columns and values with minimal lossy preprocessing. It also proposes a new evaluation suite for multi-table time-series synthetic EHRs covering fidelity, inter-table relationships, temporal dynamics, and privacy, validated on MIMIC-IV and eICU against several baseline generators. SDV is used as one of three multi-table baselines, run via its Hierarchical ML Algorithm (HMA) synthesizer with Gaussian Copulas at default hyperparameters, and is consistently outperformed by RawMed on fidelity, utility, and temporal metrics.

paper-accessibility-barriers-causal-2025.summary: Generates synthetic categorical survey data through causal graph models, arguing that preserving causal structure matters more than matching marginals when the downstream use is causal inference about accessibility barriers. Gaussian copula and CTGAN are the alternatives the Bayesian network method is compared against.

paper-hybrid-framework-generating-realis.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid AI framework combining an LSTM architecture with deep-learning generative models and statistical techniques to synthesize multivariate, time-dependent network flow data for cybersecurity digital twins, aiming to support intrusion-detection training and validation. The synthetic data generation pipeline blends sequence-aware neural modeling with statistical synthesis of numerical and categorical features to preserve realistic attack/normal traffic proportions. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, apparently as a foundational reference for its statistical/generative data-synthesis approach, though the extent of any actual SDV library use is not confirmed from the available evidence.
paper-hybrid-framework-generating-realis.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV library/synthesizer was actually run or only cited as background for the statistical synthesis component.

paper-learning-priority-assignment-prefe.summary: This paper proposes a learning-based framework for reverse-engineering task priorities from historical scheduling data, combining CTGAN-based data augmentation, Bayesian-network preference modeling, a GAN-based priority-learning module, and constraint-relaxation optimization, validated on a surgical operating-room scheduling case study. CTGAN is trained on real scheduling records to correct class imbalance among surgeon/surgery types, using its conditional sampling mechanism to target rare categories, and its augmented data is compared against SMOTE and TVAE for correlation preservation. CTGAN (and TVAE as a comparison baseline) from the SDV/CTGAN family is run directly as the core data-augmentation generator underpinning the empirical pipeline.

paper-metrics-inter-dataset-similarity-2.summary: Proposes two novel PCA-based metrics (difference in explained variance and angle difference) for measuring inter-dataset similarity, and demonstrates their use in evaluating synthetic data utility and feature-selection performance. The synthetic-data experiments generate benchmark datasets with several generators, including TVAE, and track how the proposed metrics evolve over training epochs and correlate with existing SynthEval metrics. TVAE, cited to the CTGAN paper and described as coming 'from CTGAN', is run as one of several synthetic data generators whose output is used to validate the new metrics.

paper-modeling-intrusion-detection-syste.summary: This conference paper proposes a hybrid Decision Tree–LSTM intrusion detection model evaluated on the CICIDS2017 dataset under three training conditions: the original imbalanced data, random over/undersampling, and CTGAN-balanced data. The hybrid model consistently achieved the highest accuracy and F1 scores under the CTGAN-balanced condition (CTGANSamp), demonstrating that synthetic minority-class samples improve detection of rare attack types. CTGAN is run as the generator producing synthetic minority-class network traffic samples used to balance one of the three training conditions compared in the study.

paper-predicting-relative-performance-am.summary: This article presents a comparative analysis of different forecasting approaches for predicting the relative performance among financial assets, evaluating multiple predictive methods within a financial-markets context. The evidence available (metadata only) does not reveal the specific methodology, experiments, or how CTGAN factors into the comparison. It cites the CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) paper, but the manner of use -- as a baseline generator, a data-augmentation tool, or a mere citation -- cannot be determined from the metadata alone.

paper-seasonal-segmentation-life-moment-.summary: This paper proposes a two-block hybrid framework combining K-means clustering (for fixed seasonal periods) and an SVM-SHAP model (for detecting unpredictable life events like home purchases) using financial transactional data, achieving 87.4% F1-score and outperforming single-model baselines. It targets customer activation, churn reduction, and mortgage conversion in financial services, with SHAP used for interpretability. CTGAN is only cited in the reference list, alongside other unrelated works, with no evidence it was used in the study's methodology or experiments.

paper-synthetic-tool-prototyping-early-2.summary: This paper is a proof-of-concept study exploring synthetic data generation to prototype machine-learning models for early-stage periodontitis detection, given the scarcity of publicly available salivary biomarker datasets. The authors train a Tabular Variational Autoencoder to expand a small seed dataset to 4,000 synthetic samples spanning inflammatory, metabolic, microbiome and demographic features across Healthy, Elevated, and Periodontitis classes, then benchmark XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and other classifiers on this synthetic data. TVAE, the tabular variational autoencoder introduced alongside CTGAN, is the sole generative model underpinning the entire empirical programme, though no specific software package or library is named, leaving whether SDV's own implementation was run unclear.

paper-tsdcg-tabular-synthetic-code-2025.summary: This paper proposes TSDCG, a method that uses code-generating LLMs combined with data profiling to synthesize tabular data faster and more cheaply than model-training-based approaches. It benchmarks TSDCG against GReaT, TVAE, and CTGAN on the iris dataset, reporting per-iteration training time and distributional similarity metrics, and claims comparable or better quality at lower cost. CTGAN and TVAE are run as baseline generators against which the authors' LLM-based TSDCG is compared.

The model is evaluated against the original CTAB-GAN+ baseline on ML utility, statistical similarity, and distance-based privacy metrics. CTGAN and its predecessor TGAN are cited only in the related-work discussion as the conditional-GAN lineage from which CTAB-GAN+ descends, with no SDV-family code run in the experiments.

paper-cle-context-aware-local-2024.summary: This paper proposes CLE, a three-step explainability framework for high-dimensional tabular data that generates synthetic local data around a data point, classifies it as near- or far-boundary, and calibrates the explanation using a surrogate model or feature attribution accordingly. It is evaluated on datasets from power systems, breast cancer, heart disease, and phishing detection, showing improved local explanations compared to LIME. CTGAN is run directly as the core synthetic data generator that produces the local samples driving the entire explanation pipeline.

paper-ctgan-enn-tabular-gan-2024.summary: This paper proposes CTGAN-ENN, a hybrid sampling framework that oversamples the minority class of imbalanced, overlapping customer-churn datasets using CTGAN and then applies Edited Nearest Neighbours (ENN) under-sampling to remove the resulting class overlap. Tested across five churn datasets (bank, mobile, telco, insurance) and several ML classifiers, CTGAN-ENN is shown to outperform SMOTE-ENN, ADASYN-ENN, WGAN-GP+ENN and cost-sensitive learning baselines. CTGAN is used as the core generator for minority-class oversampling, run via the published ctgan Python package, and its mode-specific handling of mixed and imbalanced categorical data is described as the mechanism enabling the oversampling stage of the proposed pipeline.

paper-evaluating-artificial-intelligence.summary: This paper evaluates five AI forecasting models (ARIMA, LSTM, random forest, gradient boosting, neural networks) and reinforcement-learning-based pricing (Q-learning, deep Q-learning) for demand-supply matching and dynamic pricing in circular-economy digital marketplaces, finding gradient boosting most effective for demand forecasting. The study relies on synthetic data for controlled experimentation, acknowledging its limits versus real-world variability, and cites the original SDV paper as a source for its synthetic data approach.

paper-metabolomic-multiclass-balance-202.summary: Balances a highly imbalanced multiclass metabolomic dataset for metabolic syndrome analysis, where the classes of clinical interest are the sparse ones. Gaussian Copula, FAST ML, CTGAN and TVAE are the evaluated models, making the comparison almost entirely internal to SDV.

paper-fairness-bias-algorithmic-hiring-2.summary: This is a multidisciplinary survey that integrates work on algorithmic hiring systems, sources of bias, fairness measures, mitigation strategies, datasets, and legal aspects of automated recruitment, aiming to give practitioners and researchers a balanced view of the field. The paper does not propose a new system but synthesizes and evaluates existing literature and datasets used in fairness research on hiring. The Synthetic Data Vault paper by Patki, Wedge, and Veeramachaneni is listed only in the reference list, with no indication in the retrieved body text that SDV software or synthetic data generation was actually used or discussed.

paper-metamaterials-rigid-inverse-design.summary: Proposes RIGID, a random-forest-based interpretable generative inverse design method that inverts a forest surrogate to sample metamaterial designs meeting qualitative targets on functional responses such as frequency-dependent behavior, in a single shot and without the large training sets and iterative optimization that deep generative approaches require. The paper's only contact with the SDV lineage is one grouped citation: Xu and Veeramachaneni's TGAN paper appears with two other mixed-type generative models to support the claim that generative and optimization-based inverse design handle mixed continuous and categorical design variables poorly. No SDV code is run and CTGAN is never named, so the entry records a bibliographic reference to TGAN, the predecessor of CTGAN, rather than any use of the SDV stack.

paper-incremental-drifting-evaluation-me.summary: This paper addresses incremental concept drift in machine learning by proposing methods to generate datasets with controlled drift types and a new protocol for evaluating a learner's knowledge transfer capability, then comparing Domain Adaptation and Lifelong Learning approaches under such drift. The work is not about tabular data synthesis itself; CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, as a one-line example noting that GANs can generate tabular data besides images, and is not run or engaged with further.

paper-perfgen-synthesis-evaluation-frame.summary: PERFGEN is a framework for synthesizing High-Performance Computing (HPC) performance data and evaluating its quality via a novel metric called Dissimilarity, aimed at reducing the burden of repeated application runs for data collection. The framework uses two generators -- CTGAN and an LLM-based GReaT model -- and compares its Dissimilarity metric against SDMetrics' SD Quality, KL-divergence, and TabSynDex on performance and general ML datasets. CTGAN is run directly as one of the two core generators (with hyperparameters like discriminator steps tuned via wandb) and extended with a custom conditioning API, while SDMetrics' quality score is used as a baseline evaluation metric.

paper-maip-encrypted-traffic-2023.summary: Presents MAIP, a GUI framework that pairs a stacked-autoencoder and CNN detector for encrypted malicious traffic with SHAP and LIME explanations and a built-in adversarial attack and defence module. CTGAN is the tabular generator behind the framework's GAN poisoning attack, exposed as its own API endpoints, and the rows it produces are also fed back as adversarial training data to answer the paper's robustness question.

CTGAN is run as the generator producing the synthetic IDS training data that the entire empirical evaluation depends on.

The CTGAN model is used throughout as the core generator, run with its conditional vector and mode normalization to produce the synthetic data that drives the entire empirical attack pipeline.

It benchmarks SDV against Synthpop and DataSynthesizer (independent and correlated attribute modes), finding no single synthesizer dominates across settings. The Synthetic Data Vault, described as offering a multivariate Gaussian Copula model, is run as one of the three data synthesizers whose generated datasets are evaluated throughout the empirical comparison.
paper-empirical-analysis-synthetic-anoma.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV was run as a generator/baseline or only cited in passing. Judged conservatively as citation_only from metadata alone.

paper-beyond-simple-images-human-2021.summary: This paper proposes human-allied GANs (HA-GAN) that incorporate expert-provided correlation advice as inductive bias to generate synthetic clinical data such as lab test values, addressing GANs' difficulty capturing feature relationships from small observational datasets. The authors evaluate their approach against several GAN variants (GAN, medGAN, medWGAN, medBGAN, CTGAN) on four clinical datasets including MIMIC and ADNI. CTGAN, described as extending GANs with mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator, is run as one of several baseline generators in the TSTR comparison table, generally underperforming the proposed method.

paper-genetic-programming-symbolic-regre.summary: This civil engineering paper develops a genetic-programming-based symbolic regression model to predict the shear capacity of steel fibre-reinforced concrete (SFRC) beams, aiming to produce an interpretable closed-form expression as an alternative to black-box machine learning models. The work is evaluated against existing empirical and ML-based prediction models using a compiled experimental database. The evidence shows only that it cites the TGAN paper, with no indication of how or whether TGAN's synthetic data generation was actually used.

paper-improving-machine-learning-diagnos.summary: This paper proposes a model-based data augmentation technique that integrates computer-implementable electromechanical models with stochastic parameter sampling to generate synthetic normal- and abnormal-condition data for machine-learning diagnostics, demonstrated on distribution transformer fault detection. The synthetic data are validated against real measurements and used to train diagnostic classifiers that outperform state-of-the-art systems, especially with scarce abnormal-condition data. CTGAN's conditional GAN architecture is cited and 'slightly modified' by the authors to generate synthetic data as part of their augmentation pipeline.

paper-smartsso-deep-learning-platform-20.summary: This paper proposes SmartSSO, a variational-autoencoder-based system for linking multiple accounts belonging to the same user within academic federated identity management environments, using login behavior embeddings when network-based social data is unavailable. Because collected real login data was limited, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault library to generate synthetic training samples, finding GANs unsuccessful and settling on SDV's Gaussian Copula model to produce 30k synthetic samples for training and evaluation. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is thus run as the actual generator underpinning the data augmentation central to the empirical results.

paper-comparison-classical-privacy-mecha.summary: This paper benchmarks classical statistical disclosure control methods (noise addition, microaggregation, rank swapping), differential privacy mechanisms, and deep-learning-based approaches (a GAN and Machine Learning Copies) for privacy-utility trade-offs on a commercial dataset, measuring Disclosure Risk and Information Loss across methods. The authors build their own GAN-based sanitization mechanism, choosing its number of hidden layers and training epochs based on settings recommended in the CTGAN paper. CTGAN is only cited for its architecture and epoch recommendations, which inform the authors' own hand-built GAN, and the SDV library itself is never invoked or run.

paper-training-testing-validation-challe.summary: This industry-perspective article discusses challenges in training, testing, and validating AI/ML systems for next-generation wireless networks, covering issues like stability, privacy, and data scarcity across use cases such as massive MIMO, RAN planning, and analytics. It is a non-technical, opinion-style piece with no experiments or implemented methods. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is only cited in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

preprint-bstabdiff-block-subunit-diffusi.summary: This paper proposes BSTabDiff, a block-subunit generative framework for tabular data in the High-Dimensional Low-Sample-Size (HDLSS) regime, such as omics data, that partitions features into latent blocks and models each block with a Gaussian-copula-driven decoder plus a diffusion or flow prior on block latents. It is evaluated against several baseline generators on eight HDLSS datasets using downstream TSTR/TRTR classification utility. CTGAN and its VAE counterpart TVAE (from the SDV-family CTGAN paper) are run as GAN- and VAE-based baseline generators in the empirical comparison, while an SDV system-based synthesizer (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in passing as prior tabular-synthesis work.
preprint-bstabdiff-block-subunit-diffusi.needs: SDV proper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in the introduction as a 'system-based generator' and never run; only CTGAN/TVAE are empirically evaluated.

preprint-improving-tabpfn-synthetic-gene.summary: This paper investigates TabPFN, an autoregressive foundation model for tabular data, showing that its feature-order dependence produces spurious correlations when it conflicts with the true causal structure, and proposes DAG-aware and PDAG-based conditioning strategies to inject causal knowledge at inference time without retraining. The methods are evaluated on controlled benchmarks and six CSuite datasets for structural fidelity, distributional quality, and treatment-effect preservation. CTGAN is included as one of five external tabular generator baselines compared against the proposed TabPFN variants, while TGAN and CTGAN are also mentioned in the related-work discussion of prior deep generative tabular models.

paper-dependency-gap-diagnostic-2026.summary: Shows that a fully factorized table, with every column shuffled independently so that all inter-column dependency is destroyed, still passes the commonly reported linear classifier two-sample test on four benchmarks, and replaces it with a gradient-boosted test whose score decomposes into marginal, dependency and numerical-categorical cross terms read against zero-dependency and oracle references. The metrics shown to be blind are SDMetrics': the logistic detection score and the pairwise Trend similarity are computed and reported throughout as the foil against which the new diagnostic is set.

paper-mobevolve-2026.summary: Generates human trip chains through a system of interpretable heuristics for travel participation, mobility retrieval and refinement that a language model agent rewrites and re-scores against held-out data, so the generator stays readable and cheap while beating deep and LLM-based mobility models on Singapore and Montreal benchmarks. Four SDV single-table synthesizers stand in for the deep tabular generative arm of the comparison, Gaussian Copula, TVAE, Copula-GAN and CTGAN, run from the SDV library and reported on individual, distribution and behaviour metrics as well as generation latency.

preprint-physics-informed-diffusion-gene.summary: This paper presents PhysDGM, a physics-embedded diffusion generative model that injects physical laws into each reverse diffusion step to synthesize physically consistent industrial time-series data for turbofan engines, aero-engines, batteries, and chemical processes. Using PhysDGM-generated synthetic data substantially improved downstream tasks like remaining useful life prediction, health indicator estimation, and fault diagnosis while requiring far less real training data. The SDV founding paper is cited only in the reference list, with no SDV component appearing or being used anywhere in the body text.

preprint-privacy-preserving-drift-detect.summary: This paper presents ProxyDrift, a Microsoft framework for detecting and correcting drift between production LLM traffic and offline evaluation sets without accessing raw user data, using non-PII proxy representations, a chance-calibrated redundancy-aware alignment score, and a Chow-Liu tree-based conditional sampler for generating synthetic proxies. It targets privacy-preserving continuous monitoring and evaluation-set refresh for large-scale LLM applications. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it is used anywhere in the text.

preprint-synthetic-generation-nonparamet.summary: This preprint proposes a nonparametric multivariate similarity test based on the Cramér-Wold theorem and random projection testing to evaluate the fidelity of a previously proposed small-sample synthetic data generator (based on decoupled transformations and kernel density estimation), applied to low-dimensional biomedical datasets such as bean and mammography data. The generator evaluated is the authors' own, not SDV; the original SDV/'Synthetic Data Vault' DSAA 2016 paper appears only as a reference-list citation among other synthetic data generation methods, with no evidence it was run or its methods engaged with in the body text.

preprint-instruction-tuning-large-langua.summary: This paper proposes instruction-tuning an open-source LLM (Llama3.1-8B-Instruct) on a curated instruction dataset to enable efficient tabular data generation, achieving performance comparable to GPT-4o with limited compute. It evaluates fidelity and utility of generated synthetic tables across several benchmark datasets using a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) protocol. CTGAN's originating paper (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only as the source of the TSTR evaluation framework, with no SDV code run.

preprint-value-digital-economy-investiga.summary: A preprint in economics examining how personal information protection regulations affect the value of data and broader economic outcomes in the digital economy. No abstract or full text was available, so the paper's methodology and findings cannot be characterized beyond its listed topic. It cites the original SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016) among its references, apparently only as a background citation rather than as a tool used in the analysis.

preprint-anogan-tabular-anomaly-detectio.summary: This preprint adapts the AnoGAN anomaly-detection framework, originally developed for images, to tabular data by first synthesizing samples with CTGAN and then applying AnoGAN's reconstruction-error scoring to distinguish anomalies from normal points. The authors identify prediction randomness in CTGAN's outputs, traced to the Gumbel Softmax activation used for categorical columns, and replace it with a 'hard' Gumbel Softmax variant to make generation more deterministic before running AnoGAN on the resulting synthetic data. CTGAN's generator architecture and its Gumbel-softmax-based categorical sampling mechanism are directly modified, and the modified generator supplies the synthetic samples underlying the entire empirical evaluation.

preprint-caps-collaborative-private-synt.summary: This paper proposes CaPS, a framework for collaboratively generating differentially private synthetic tabular data from distributed data holders, replacing the trusted aggregator with secure multi-party computation (MPC) protocols and combining this with differential privacy for output privacy. It demonstrates scalability and applicability for state-of-the-art marginal-based select-measure-generate algorithms MWEM+PGM and AIM. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only as an example of a GAN-based approach to differentially private synthetic data generation, contrasted with the marginal-based methods the paper actually studies.

preprint-derec-simpro-unlock-language-20.summary: Proposes DEREC, a pre-processing pipeline that converts many-to-many collaborative table relationships into one-to-many form, paired with SIMPRO, a 3-aspect evaluation suite using conditional distributions and large-scale hypothesis testing, to improve multi-table data synthesis in Data Clean Room settings. The authors benchmark their DEREC-REaLTabFormer model against single-table CT-GAN/TabDDPM and against the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) multi-table synthesizer, and repeatedly use SDMetrics scores to audit synthetic fidelity, showing SDMetrics can favor 'smoothed' SDV output over visually better REaLTabFormer output. SDV is run as a multi-table synthesizer baseline, CT-GAN as a single-table baseline, and SDMetrics' quality-report scoring is used throughout as the comparative evaluation metric.

paper-rebalancing-smote-variants-2024.summary: Analyses SMOTE and its descendants theoretically, showing where interpolation-based oversampling does and does not help, and pairs that with a broad empirical comparison that includes the case of applying no rebalancing at all, arguing that the default assumption in favour of rebalancing is weaker than practice suggests. CTGAN is run as the deep generative arm of that comparison and is described in its own subsection, with the study reporting that it performs significantly worse than applying no strategy at all on three of the datasets.

preprint-enhancing-deep-knowledge-tracin.summary: This preprint proposes using TabDDPM, a diffusion model, to generate synthetic educational records that augment training data for Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) in personalized adaptive learning, validated on ASSISTments datasets. The actual generative pipeline runs TabDDPM, not any SDV-family model. CTGAN is only cited in passing, in a related-work sentence and reference list, as an example of GAN-based tabular data generation.

preprint-representation-debiasing-genera.summary: This preprint proposes human-in-the-loop interaction approaches that let domain experts steer and validate data augmentation algorithms to mitigate representation bias in AI training datasets. It argues for a controlled, expert-guided data generation process rather than fully automated debiasing, aiming toward user-centred AI systems. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited among prior work on synthetic/generated data, with no indication SDV software was run.

paper-overlap-class-imbalanced-2024.summary: Splits the majority class into a clear part and an overlap part lying on the minority boundary, trains a class-conditional generator on the resulting three-way labels, and then drops the overlap class when assembling the classifier's training mix, reporting consistent gains for imbalanced tabular classification across four datasets and five classifiers. The procedure is applied on top of five generators, CTGAN among them, which is run conditionally on the ternary labels and reported both with and without the treatment.

preprint-codi-evolving-contrastive-diffu.summary: This paper proposes CoDi, two co-evolving conditional diffusion models with contrastive training that process continuous and discrete tabular columns separately yet jointly, aiming to better preserve inter-column correlations than prior tabular synthesis methods. It is evaluated against 8 baseline generators (including MedGAN, VEEGAN, TableGAN, OCT-GAN, RNODE, STaSy, CTGAN and TVAE) across 11 real-world datasets on quality, diversity, and sampling-time metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run throughout as two of several comparison baselines, while SDV's Patki et al. (2016) recursive Gaussian-copula table modeling is cited only in the related-work discussion as prior art.

paper-missdiff-missing-values-2023.summary: Trains diffusion models directly on tables that contain missing values, masking the regression loss for unobserved entries so the score is learned without first imputing, and shows the resulting estimator is consistent under missing-at-random assumptions where impute-then-generate pipelines are not. CTGAN and TVAE appear once, inside the paper's description of a diffusion baseline reported to outperform them by a large margin; neither is run here.

preprint-qualitative-augmentation-perfor.summary: This preprint proposes using GANs to generate synthetic circuit performance data to augment small training datasets for analog and digital VLSI machine-learning models, drawing training data from Cadence Virtuoso, HSPICE, and Microcap simulations and showing large reductions in prediction error. The work is a general survey-and-experiment paper on GAN-based data augmentation for circuit design, not on tabular synthetic data specifically. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthesizing tabular data with GANs, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the body text.

preprint-synthetic-dataset-generation-me.summary: This preprint proposes a methodology to synthesize recommender-system datasets by combining Gaussian copulas (implemented from scratch via Cholesky decomposition) for numerical/ordinal features, a Dirichlet-Multinomial model for nominal features, a Multinomial Logit model for latent user preferences, and a Fuzzy Inference System to generate ratings. The Gaussian copula and other statistical techniques are mathematically derived and implemented by the author rather than drawn from any software package. The metadata indicates a citation to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, but no passage in the extracted body text shows CTGAN being run, described, or engaged with beyond a bibliographic reference.

preprint-partially-synthetic-recommender.summary: This paper investigates statistical disclosure control for recommender systems, using a CART-based partial synthesis method to transform a user-item matrix so that some attributes are hidden while relative algorithm performance is preserved. Experiments on recommender datasets show the partially synthesized data supports algorithm ranking comparable to the original data while obscuring specific user preference information. The paper cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper in its related-work references on synthetic data generation, but does not run or engage with SDV software.

preprint-synthetic-observational-health-.summary: This is a broad literature review surveying published GAN applications for Observational Health Data, cataloguing algorithms, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility practices across dozens of papers such as medGAN, HealthGAN, and EMR-WGAN. It discusses SDV as a listed technique in its comparative tables and glossary, describing it as 'a generative model for relational database based on Gaussian Copulas' and noting HealthGAN adapts SDV's data transformation to map categorical features to the unit range. SDV's Gaussian-copula relational model and CTGAN's mode-specific normalization are both described in prose as prior methods used by other reviewed works, but neither is run by the authors themselves.

SDV's demo loader and CTGAN are run as the seminar's synthetic-data example.
